primary_source_citation.title: CFPB & Federal Reserve Education Technical Reference: 13-Week Zero-Based Cash-Flow Budget & Needs vs. Wants

1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Pay yourself first by allocating 10 to 20 percent of every income receipt into savings before discretionary spending.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Record Expected 13-Week Income: List every predictable dollar: part-time job wages, lawn/babysitting earnings, and regular allowance.
2. Allocate Savings & Fixed Needs First: Deduct automatic savings (20 percent) and non-negotiable expenses (camp fees, transit, school dues) first.
3. Log Every Daily Receipt Honestly: Record actual cash and debit transactions within 24 hours so small impulse purchases never hide.
4. Reconcile Weekly Surplus or Deficit: Compare Planned vs. Actual every Sunday and adjust variable wants so Net Cash Flow stays >= $0.
1.worked_field_example: On $40 of weekly lawn-mowing income over 13 weeks ($520 total), saving 20 percent ($8 per week) builds a $104 camp gear fund automatically.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: Divide ten $1 tokens across Save, Needs, and Goals jars before logging a sample week in the 13-week ledger.
1.real_world_connection_box: CFPB & Federal Reserve Zero-Based Budget Standard: Pay yourself first by allocating 10 to 20 percent of every income receipt into savings before discretionary spending.
1.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + CFPB & Federal Reserve Personal Finance
1.bespoke_visual_caption: Personal budgeting flat-lay with three icon-labeled savings jars, a 13-week tracking ledger, fountain pen, and compass.
1.v47_slide_title: CFPB & Federal Reserve Zero-Based Budget Standard

primary_source_citation.title: FINRA Foundation & SEC Investor.gov Technical Reference: Saving vs. Investing: Risk, Liquidity & Diversification Matrix

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Expected long-term return scales directly with investment volatility from insured bank savings and Treasury bonds to diversified stock index funds.
core_mechanism_bullets: FDIC Bank Savings & CDs (Low Risk): Insured up to $250,000 per depositor; immediate liquidity for emergency funds and near-term goals.
U.S. Treasury & Savings Bonds: Loan to the U.S. government paying fixed interest over a stated maturity; backed by full faith and credit.
Broad Stock Index Funds (Diversified): Owns hundreds of companies in one single low-fee basket so one single bankruptcy never wipes out savings.
Individual Stocks (Concentrated Equity): Ownership share in one company; highest single-firm volatility alongside long-term earnings growth potential.
3.worked_field_example: Holding a broad S&P 500 index fund spreads company risk across 500 businesses while FDIC savings protect emergency cash needed within 12 months.
3.counselor_tabletop_demo: Place four Scout financial goals (next month's campout vs. a 10-year vehicle or college fund) onto the four steps of the risk-return ladder.
3.real_world_connection_box: SEC Investor.gov & FINRA Risk-Return Standard: Expected long-term return scales directly with investment volatility from insured bank savings and Treasury bonds to diversified stock index funds.
3.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + SEC Investor.gov & FINRA
3.bespoke_visual_caption: Four ascending investment steps progressing from an insured bank vault and bond scroll to a diversified basket and high-growth rocket.
v47_primary_source_bullets: Expected long-term return scales directly with investment volatility from insured bank savings and Treasury bonds to diversified stock index funds.

primary_source_citation.title: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) Technical Reference: APR, Credit Reports & Avoiding the Minimum-Payment Debt Trap

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Divide 72 by the annual compound interest rate to find the exact number of years required to double your money.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Charge Card / Full Statement Payoff: Pay 100 percent of statement balance before due date: $0 interest charged and builds strong payment history.
2. Revolving Credit Card Balance (22% APR): Paying only the 2 percent minimum on $2,000 takes over 9 years and costs more than $2,100 in extra interest.
3. Five Pillars of FICO Credit Score: Payment history (35%), credit utilization under 10-30% (30%), credit age (15%), mix (10%), new inquiries (10%).
4. Comparison Shopping Major Purchases: Calculate Total Out-the-Door Cost (price + tax + financing interest + insurance + maintenance) before buying.
4.worked_field_example: At an 8 percent annual compound return, 72 divided by 8 equals 9 years per doubling, turning $1,000 into $2,000 in 9 years and $4,000 in 18 years.
4.counselor_tabletop_demo: Calculate how many times a $500 investment doubles between age 14 and age 50 at 8 percent compound growth (four doublings to $8,000).
4.real_world_connection_box: SEC & Federal Reserve Rule of 72 Standard: Divide 72 by the annual compound interest rate to find the exact number of years required to double your money.
4.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + SEC Investor.gov Compound Interest Guide
4.bespoke_visual_caption: Visual comparison of flat linear simple interest versus exponential compound doubling over four consecutive periods.
4.v47_slide_title: SEC & Federal Reserve Rule of 72 Standard
v47_primary_source_bullets: Divide 72 by the annual compound interest rate to find the exact number of years required to double your money.
